{"description":"WHY THIS EXISTS. The session of 2026-09-22 delivered three merged PRs against an ordering Anthony approved, then produced four brainstorms in a row and followed each one. He named it: "I feel like there were some previous tasks we were doing before this latest round of brainstorming… let's not get de-railed by going off in tangent after tangent." Two steps of the approved ordering were never started, and the brainstorms produced measured blockers that nothing is scheduled against. This epoch is the list.

🛑 WHAT THIS EPOCH IS NOT: it is not a decision to build the x/y composability architecture. Three open questions came out of this session and NONE has Anthony's word. The buildable items below were chosen because they are measured defects that every one of those options sits on — so they pay for themselves whichever way the questions are settled, and they are the honest thing to do BEFORE settling them.

═══ THE ORDER, AND WHY IT IS THIS ORDER ═══

1. **FINISH #568.** The published-surface detector and reflow2's first six published requirements. In flight; core gates green.

2. **`mirror_surface` CANNOT REFRESH — fix it.** Measured 2026-08-12 and reproduced in the record: re-mirroring a design you already hold collides with itself (12 of 13 ids refused), leaves the STALE node in place, leaves the host's edge pointing at it, and leaves `mirrors` REPORTING THE OLD PIN — so the staleness register reads FRESH after a failed refresh. ⭐ THIS IS THE SINGLE THING EVERY COMPOSITION OPTION RESTS ON: a federation of independently-moving projects is made of refreshes. It is also live for a real consumer right now — flo2's mirror of reflow2 is pinned at 2026-08-26, roughly forty releases back, and nothing in flo2 can tell. Three open questions remain unanswerable until a mirror can be kept current, so this is first whatever is decided.
   ⚠️ NOT ESTABLISHED and to be settled as part of the work: whether a refresh should REPLACE, MERGE, or REFUSE-AND-REPORT; what happens to a host edge whose foreign target was renamed or withdrawn (reflow2 now refuses dangling edges outright); and whether the host's committed export should CARRY mirrored nodes or merely NAME them by pin.

3. **`export_surface` CARRIES NO VERIFICATIONS — decide whether it should.** Delivery is computed as satisfied AND realized AND a passing check, so THE EVIDENCE IS EXACTLY THE PART THAT CANNOT CROSS A DESIGN BOUNDARY. Consequences already named: a parent tier can compute nothing about its children (the y-axis roll-up), and an independent test-and-evaluation organisation cannot publish the one thing it exists to produce (the x-axis, in Anthony's A5/A3 framing). Pairs naturally with #568, which just made a published surface carry INTENT for the first time; this is the same question for EVIDENCE.

4. **STEP 3 OF THE APPROVED ORDERING, never started: the loop-closure reading.** Fold into `where-am-i` and `loop_status` the reading that says whether the founding chain has actually been walked. `fact:every-link-of-the-founding-chain-exists-as-a-tool-and-the-chain-has-never-been-walked-on-reflow2-itself` measured it this session: every link exists as a served tool, 311 checks read passing, and ZERO have ever been recorded failing — so the loop's entry point has never fired.

5. **STEP 4 OF THE APPROVED ORDERING, never started: the doubt-and-fork layer.** `cap:revise-trigger` and `cap:fork-alternatives` — negative feedback raises doubt against a design choice and a decision point can be returned to. Anthony's own sequencing condition stands: this waits until failing checks actually flow, which is step 4's dependency on step 3.

6. **THE STANDING DEBT, carried not scheduled: 184 capabilities still rest on a claim nothing implements.** The ratchet forbids a 185th and the set may only shrink. Deliberately NOT a task here — `dec:a-capability-may-not-newly-reach-verified-on-a-claim-alone` says grandfather it and guard forward, and writing 184 tests to move a number is the behaviour the number exists to detect.

═══ WHAT NEEDS ANTHONY'S WORD BEFORE ANY OF IT IS BUILDABLE ═══

Three questions from this session, all `proposed`, all scheduled against this epoch:
  · `dec:idea-should-realizes-stop-being-a-wildcard` — should REALIZES stop being `to: "*"`, which is what let a wrong edge be written onto 47 checks? Smallest of the three; needs the other 38 wildcard uses judged first.
  · `dec:idea-a-graph-whose-children-are-themselves-reflow2-designs` — the dev_reflow hub, sharpened into a tiered organisation with a responsible person per tier (the y-axis). Its unanswered hole: if a tier owner accepts a requirement inside a child, whose word is that? `rule:design-intent-moves-only-on-the-owners-word` is ENFORCED and checked in CI, and it would need to know.
  · `dec:idea-design-is-composable-on-two-axes-authority-and-role` — the x/y framing, sharpened by Anthony's A5/A3 experience into a LIFECYCLE axis whose stages have different owners, with "tossing it over the fence" as the named failure.

AND FIVE SMALLER ITEMS STILL AWAITING HIS WORD FROM EARLIER IN THE SAME SESSION, recorded so they do not go quiet: widening the prohibition detector past its modal blind spot; which F29 option; the both-representations measurement; whether flo2's report should be registered; and whether positive feedback should strengthen a design choice, which this agent argued against rather than accepted.

⚠️ THE HONEST NOTE ON SCOPE, and it is Anthony's own standing position: the composition questions are a large generalisation from a two-project need, and the one composition mechanism that already ships has been kept ONCE on a real pair in six weeks. Items 2 and 3 are chosen precisely because they are true whatever is decided; items beyond them should not start until the questions are settled.
